title: A Ray of Hope
content:
For a few long moments, neither of them moved.

The chilly mountain breeze continued to flow around them, carrying with it a silence that neither of them had the courage to break.

Sneha was the first to return to her senses.

As she realized how close she had come to Siddu, her cheeks instantly turned crimson. She quickly stepped back, avoiding his eyes.

"I... I'm sorry," she whispered softly.

There was no response.

Siddu stood motionless, his gaze fixed somewhere beyond the snow-covered mountains. It wasn't that he had ignored her apology—he simply hadn't heard it. His mind had already drifted into a distant memory, replaying fragments of a past that still refused to let him go.

Sneha noticed the emptiness in his eyes.

Realizing that he was lost in thought, she decided not to mention what had happened moments ago. Instead, she forced a small smile and gently changed the subject.

"Can we go?"

Her voice pulled Siddu back to reality.

He blinked once before looking at her.

"Sure," he replied quietly.

They resumed walking along the snow-covered trail.

Neither of them spoke.

The silence between them wasn't awkward anymore. It carried unspoken emotions that neither of them was ready to express.

Sneha walked a few steps behind Siddu, and every time the memory of that almost-kiss flashed through her mind, she couldn't stop herself from blushing. A shy smile unknowingly found its way onto her face before she quickly looked away, hoping Siddu hadn't noticed.

After walking for several minutes, they reached a peaceful spot overlooking the valley. Snow-covered peaks stretched endlessly before them, while soft clouds drifted lazily below, making it seem as though they were standing above the sky itself.

Sneha looked around with admiration before turning toward Siddu.

"I think this is the perfect place for our discussion."

Siddu glanced at the breathtaking view and nodded gently.

"Yeah... this place is perfect."

The two of them settled down on a large rock overlooking the mountains.

For a brief moment, neither of them spoke.

Then Sneha turned toward him with an encouraging smile.

"So..."

"Continue the story."

Siddu drew a slow, deep breath.

After remaining silent for a few seconds, he finally began.

________________________________________

"After a brief silence, Rohini finally said the words I had been dreading."

"'Shreya is in a relationship with Karthik.'"

"It felt like the world around me had suddenly stopped."

"I couldn't believe what I had just heard."

"Those words kept echoing inside my head."

"'Shreya... is in a relationship with Karthik.'"

"I felt completely shattered."

"But even then..."

"A tiny part of me still refused to believe it."

"I immediately asked Rohini to let me speak with Shreya."

"But she told me that Shreya wasn't there."

"I didn't know what else to do."

"So I asked if she had any other phone number."

"Without asking any questions, Rohini gave me another number. I thanked her, ended the call, and stared at the screen for a few seconds before gathering the courage to dial it."

Siddu paused for a moment.

His eyes remained fixed on the endless mountains before him.

"The only hope I had while dialling that number..."

"...was that Shreya herself would answer."

"And tell me that everything Rohini had said was false."

"That she wasn't in a relationship with Karthik."

"That there had been some misunderstanding."

He let out a faint smile.

"I held on to that hope..."

"And made the call."

"The phone rang."

"My heart was pounding so hard that I could hear it."

"Every second felt like an eternity."

"Then..."

"The call connected."

"I softly said..."

"'Hello...'"

A gentle smile appeared on Siddu's face as the memory unfolded before him.

"The very next moment..."

"She spoke."

"'Thank God you called this number!'"

"'I missed you so much, Rah!'"

Her voice was overflowing with happiness.

For a moment, I was completely confused.

The same girl who had ignored every one of my calls...

The same girl who had blocked my number...

Was now speaking as though she had been waiting to hear my voice all along.
